candidate_evidence.quote: Patients whose tumor was completely removed at the time of initial surgery receive WP1066 orally (PO) for 6 weeks during routine radiation therapy

target_engagement_planned_evidence.quote: Assess systemic immunological responses and phosphorylated (p)-STAT3 inhibition in patients with glioblastoma.
To ascertain the changes induced in the tumor microenvironment by the combination of WP1066 and radiation.

role_evidence.quote: Patients whose tumor was completely removed at the time of initial surgery receive WP1066 orally (PO) for 6 weeks during routine radiation therapy

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: The study drug WP1066 targets a specific pathway, known as STAT3, which is responsible for promoting tumor growth and causing the body's immune system to avoid attacking the tumor.

Assess systemic immunological responses and phosphorylated (p)-STAT3 inhibition in patients with glioblastoma.

coder_notes: Two non-randomised cohorts defined by extent of resection (Cohort 1 gross total resection, Cohort 2 not), both on WP1066 plus radiotherapy; no comparator. MGMT-unmethylated status is required for entry but is not linked to WP1066 (not candidate-matched). p-STAT3 inhibition is a secondary pharmacodynamic endpoint, so target engagement coded yes; not an entry biomarker.
